ai-agent.title: What an AI agent is
ai-agent.description: An LLM plus tools, state, and a control loop — not a chat box that “feels autonomous.”

steps.heading: Plain chat
steps.caption: Chatbot — one request, one completion, no side effects. The world outside the API call is untouched.

steps.heading: Minimal agent runtime
steps.caption: Agent — the same LLM sits inside a loop that can call tools and update durable state before answering.

steps.heading: Required pieces
steps.caption: Three ingredients — policy (LLM), tools (APIs), state (what happened so far). Remove any one and you are back to a chatbot or a script.

steps.heading: Runtime controls
steps.caption: Hard constraints live outside the model — budgets, allowlists, and human gates. Autonomy without them is an incident.

agentic-vs-chatbot.title: Agentic systems vs chatbots
agentic-vs-chatbot.description: Side effects, multi-step control, and durable state — the practical differences that matter in production.

steps.heading: Chatbot
steps.caption: Chatbot boundary — text in, text out. Advice can be wrong, but it cannot refund money by itself.

steps.heading: Agent with side effects
steps.caption: Agent boundary — tools can charge cards, send email, or delete rows. The blast radius is the tool surface.

steps.heading: One agent run vs one chat turn
steps.caption: Multi-step — agents chain observations across calls; chatbots usually reset or only append chat turns without tool results.

steps.heading: Fit check
steps.caption: Choose deliberately — if you only need wording help, a chatbot is simpler and safer. Agents earn their complexity when work requires tools.

plan-act-observe.title: Plan → Act → Observe
plan-act-observe.description: The basic control cycle: propose what to do, do it, read the result, repeat until done.

steps.heading: Planning step
steps.caption: Plan — given the goal and current state, choose the next action (often a tool name + arguments).

steps.heading: Action execution
steps.caption: Act — the runtime executes the planned tool. The model does not run the tool; your code does.

steps.heading: State after observation
steps.caption: Observe — append the tool result to state/context so the next plan sees reality, not a guess.

steps.heading: Cycle
steps.caption: Repeat or halt — either plan another act, or emit a final answer when the goal is met or the budget is exhausted.

agent-state.title: Agent state
agent-state.description: What the runtime remembers between steps — messages, scratchpad, tool results, and control flags.

steps.heading: Example state keys
steps.caption: State schema — a typed object the runtime owns, not free-form “whatever the model said.”

steps.heading: After tools.orders.get
steps.caption: Step updates — only some fields change. Highlighting diffs makes debugging possible.

steps.heading: Projected into the model window
steps.caption: Context projection — you rarely dump the entire state into the prompt; you select a view the model needs now.

steps.heading: Guard the write path
steps.caption: Corruption modes — invented tool results written into state, or status stuck on running forever.

planning.title: Planning
planning.description: Deciding a sequence of actions up front versus choosing one step at a time — and when each fails.

steps.heading: Up-front plan
steps.caption: Open-loop plan — list steps 1…n before acting. Fast to read, brittle if step 2’s observation invalidates step 3.

steps.heading: Plan meets observation
steps.caption: World disagrees — order is already refunded. Steps 3–4 of the frozen plan are now harmful.

steps.heading: Re-plan each cycle
steps.caption: Closed-loop — re-plan after each observation. Slightly more model calls, far fewer irreversible mistakes.

steps.heading: Practical pattern
steps.caption: Hybrid — sketch a coarse plan for the user, execute step-wise with checkpoints on risky tools.

memory.title: Agent memory
memory.description: Working memory in the prompt vs long-term stores — different lifetimes, different failure modes.

steps.heading: This request’s window
steps.caption: Working memory — recent messages and scratchpad inside the current run’s context.

steps.heading: Write then read across sessions
steps.caption: Long-term memory — write durable facts to a store; later runs retrieve them explicitly.

steps.heading: Memory kinds
steps.caption: Types of long-term memory — episodic (what happened), semantic (facts), procedural (how we do X).

steps.heading: Memory bugs
steps.caption: Failure modes — writing hallucinations into memory, or retrieving irrelevant memories that steer the agent wrong.

tools-tool-calling.title: Tools and tool calling
tools-tool-calling.description: Structured function calls — schemas in, validated arguments out — instead of hoping free text stays parseable.

steps.heading: Tool schema
steps.caption: Declare tools — name, description, and JSON Schema for arguments. The model only sees this catalogue.

steps.heading: Proposal vs validation
steps.caption: Model proposes a call — structured args, not prose. Invalid JSON or wrong types fail before execution.

steps.heading: Tool round-trip
steps.caption: Execute and return — runtime calls the API, then appends a tool result message for the next model turn.

steps.heading: Calls gated in one day (illustrative)
steps.caption: Reject dangerous calls — unknown tools, out-of-policy amounts, or missing confirmation never reach the network.

react-agents.title: ReAct agents
react-agents.description: Thought → Action → Observation as a runtime loop with stop sequences, parsers, and budgets — not just a prompt style.

steps.heading: Trace fragment
steps.caption: Format — the model emits Thought and Action lines; Observation is reserved for the runtime.

steps.heading: ReAct cycle
steps.caption: Loop — each Action triggers a real tool; each Observation changes the next Thought.

steps.heading: ReAct cycle 2
steps.caption: Second cycle — policy uses the observation, then may act again or finish with Final Answer.

steps.heading: Runtime checklist
steps.caption: Runtime responsibilities — parse, validate, budget, and never let the model invent Observation text.

multi-agent.title: Multi-agent systems
multi-agent.description: Multiple specialised policies sharing a protocol — useful when roles diverge, costly when they thrash.

steps.heading: Role split
steps.caption: Split roles — researcher gathers evidence; writer drafts; critic checks claims. Each has different tools.

steps.heading: Handoff
steps.caption: Protocol — agents communicate via structured messages or a shared blackboard, not vibes in one mega-context.

steps.heading: Illustrative cost of ungoverned debate
steps.caption: Failure mode — agents debate forever or overwrite each other’s artifacts without a termination rule.

steps.heading: When to split
steps.caption: Use when specialisation or parallel work pays for coordination. Otherwise one well-tooled agent is simpler.

supervisor-pattern.title: Supervisor pattern
supervisor-pattern.description: A router agent delegates to specialists and aggregates results — central control with clear ownership.

steps.heading: Routing
steps.caption: Supervisor sees the goal and the catalogue of workers — it does not do all the work itself.

steps.heading: Scoped call
steps.caption: Delegation — worker runs with a scoped prompt and tools; returns a structured result, not a free chat dump.

steps.heading: Two-worker run
steps.caption: Aggregate — supervisor may call another worker or answer the user. It owns the final response.

steps.heading: Route accuracy on a labeled set
steps.caption: Mis-routing — wrong worker selection is the characteristic bug. Log route decisions and test them.

guardrails.title: Agent guardrails
guardrails.description: Deterministic checks around a probabilistic policy — input, tool, and output gates.

steps.heading: Ingress
steps.caption: Input gate — refuse or redact dangerous user content before it reaches the model or tools.

steps.heading: refund.create checks
steps.caption: Tool gate — allowlist, argument bounds, and confirmation for irreversible actions.

steps.heading: Egress
steps.caption: Output gate — scan the final answer for secrets, disallowed topics, or missing citations before it ships.

steps.heading: Layers
steps.caption: Defence in depth — prompt policy + tool gate + output scanner. Any single layer can fail.

mcp-conceptual.title: MCP (conceptual)
mcp-conceptual.description: Model Context Protocol — a standard way for hosts to expose tools and resources to models.

steps.heading: Before
steps.caption: Problem — every tool integration reinvented its own schema and transport. Agents drowned in one-off adapters.

steps.heading: Roles
steps.caption: MCP server — advertises tools/resources with schemas; host connects and calls them via the protocol.

steps.heading: Session sketch
steps.caption: Discover then call — list tools, show schemas to the model, execute selected tool through the host.

steps.heading: Host responsibilities
steps.caption: Still your threat model — a malicious or over-privileged MCP server is a tool-exfiltration risk.

hitl.title: Human-in-the-loop
hitl.description: Pause the agent for approval on risky steps — resume with an explicit human decision recorded in state.

steps.heading: Pause point
steps.caption: Trigger — policy wants refund.create for $480. Guardrail requires a human because amount > threshold.

steps.heading: Approval card
steps.caption: Human UI — show the proposed call, evidence, and consequences. Approve, edit args, or reject.

steps.heading: Outcomes
steps.caption: Resume — approval writes a signed decision into state; runtime executes; rejection ends or re-plans.

steps.heading: Async HITL
steps.caption: Design for latency — humans are slow. Persist checkpoints and notify; do not hold an HTTP request open for hours.

checkpointing.title: Checkpointing
checkpointing.description: Persist run state so crashes, deploys, and HITL pauses do not lose the thread.

steps.heading: Crash
steps.caption: Without checkpoints — process dies after tool 2; restart either skips work or repeats side effects blindly.

steps.heading: Write cadence
steps.caption: Checkpoint after each durable step — write state + last completed node to storage before the next risk.

steps.heading: Recovery
steps.caption: Resume — load snapshot, skip completed idempotent tools, continue from the cursor.

steps.heading: Snapshot contents
steps.caption: What to store — enough to rebuild the prompt and avoid duplicate side effects; not necessarily full HTTP traces forever.

agent-failure-modes.title: Agent failure modes
agent-failure-modes.description: Loops, tool misuse, hallucinated observations, and goal drift — each needs a different control.

steps.heading: Repeated tool signature detector
steps.caption: Infinite loop — the same Action with the same args repeats until timeout.

steps.heading: Schema-valid, policy-invalid
steps.caption: Tool misuse — wrong tool or args that pass schema but violate business rules.

steps.heading: Authenticity
steps.caption: Hallucinated observation — model writes what it wished the tool returned. Only the runtime may author Observation.

steps.heading: Drift example
steps.caption: Goal drift — after many steps the agent optimises a side quest. Keep the goal string pinned in state and prompts.
